Admissions for Graduate Programs
The USC Mathematics Department is a dynamic community of scholars, innovators, and educators dedicated to mathematical excellence and advancing mathematical understanding. We take immense pride in our supportive research environment.
We seek all applicants who share our vision of and passion for mathematics. All applications require 3 letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, a short resumé or CV, official transcripts, and TOEFL scores (international applicants only). We do not require GRE tests.
FAQ
Apply Now
Application Deadline: December 15
Ph.D. Programs
Our department offers two doctoral degree programs:
Mathematics Ph.D.
Applied Mathematics Ph.D.
Our rigorous 5-year program begins with foundational coursework that prepares students to demonstrate mastery through written comprehensive examinations. After this, students work closely with one of our distinguished research faculty to reach the frontier of knowledge in their chosen field. Thus equipped and with ongoing guidance from their advisor, students forge a path to new results through original research. The program culminates with the student’s written dissertation, oral defense, and the conferral of Doctorate of Philosophy.
Admission to our Ph.D. programs includes a 5-year aid package with 1 year of fellowship, 4 years of teaching assistantship, full tuition remission, plus health and dental insurance.
Applicants who attended the 2026 NAM Undergraduate MathFest are eligible for a fee waiver. Please email your NAM MathFest registration confirmation to Alexis Teodoro (ateodoro@usc.edu) to receive a letter with instructions on how to obtain the fee waiver. Because of the volume of requests, the approval process may require 3-4 business days. For this reason, we strongly advise you to submit your fee waiver request as early as possible and well in advance of the application deadline.
Apply through the Office of Graduate Admission
Masters Programs
We offer six different Masters programs. The application deadline for Masters Programs vary:
Fall Admission Cycle – Apply by February 1
Applications open on September 1. All programs have a deadline of February 1, except the Mathematical Data Science M.S. (February 15) and the Mathematical Finance M.S. (March 30).
Spring Admission Cycle – Apply by October 15
Applications open on August 1. All programs have a deadline of October 15.
CONTACT INFORMATION
For more information, please fill out this form.
For questions about admission: masters_admissions@dornsife.usc.edu
To reach an academic advisor: masters_advising@dornsife.usc.edu

Admissions FAQs
When is the application deadline?
The application deadline for the PhD Programs is December 15. This is a hard deadline, and we cannot accept materials submitted to us after this deadline.
The application deadline for Fall admission Masters Programs is February 1, except the Mathematical Data Science M.S. (February 15) and the Mathematical Finance M.S. (March 30).
The application deadline for Spring admission Masters Programs is October 15.
Can I get a waiver for the application fee?
The mathematics department does NOT offer fee waivers for students.
However, applicants who attended the 2026 NAM Undergraduate MathFest are eligible for a fee waiver. Please email your NAM MathFest registration confirmation to Alexis Teodoro (ateodoro@usc.edu) to receive a letter with instructions on how to obtain the fee waiver. Because of the volume of requests, the approval process may require 3-4 business days. For this reason, we strongly advise you to submit your fee waiver request as early as possible and well in advance of the application deadline.
Additionally, the USC Graduate Admissions Office has several categories of applicants who qualify for fee waivers. To see if you qualify, please visit this website: https://gradadm.usc.edu/lightboxes/us-students-fee-waivers/
Is there financial aid available for the programs?
Yes for PhD, No for Masters.
Everyone, regardless of nationality or country of residence, admitted to our PhD Programs receives a comprehensive support package that includes full tuition remission, a competitive stipend, and health and dental insurance.
We do not offer any financial assistance for our Masters programs. We encourage all Masters applicants who are California residents to apply for California State graduate fellowships.
What are the English Proficiency requirements?
U.S. citizens and legal permanent residents are exempt. For other exemption qualifications, please see
https://gradadm.usc.edu/prospective-international-students/english-proficiency/
For international students requiring English Proficiency tests, we require a minimum of
100 on TOEFL or
7.0 on IELTS or
68 on PTE.
These minima apply to both PhD and Masters programs.
Is a Masters degree required before applying for the PhD program?
Not at all! The majority of our incoming PhD students, about 2/3, come from Bachelor’s programs while the remaining 1/3 come from Masters programs.
All of our Ph.D. students have the opportunity to earn an “in progress” Masters degree, which is usually conferred in the second year of the program after satisfactory completion of the core course requirements. Students in either PhD program may choose between a Masters Degree in Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, or Statistics.
Is there a minimum GPA requirement for admission?
Yes. We require applicants to have an undergraduate GPA above 3.0.
The minimum GPA requirement for a student to receive a graduate degree, Masters or Doctorate, from USC is 3.0. For this reason, we will not consider any applicants whose undergraduate GPA falls below this minimum threshold.
For the Fall 2025 PhD Admissions cycle, the average GPA of admitted students was 3.89 with a standard deviation of 0.18.
Are there any specific courses that are required for admission?
Yes, and requirements vary by program.
Every applicant is required to have two terms* of advanced Analysis (real, complex, or functional). Applicants for our Mathematics programs are also required to have two terms* of advanced Algebra (abstract or linear). Some of these courses can be planned for your final semester.
*In general, one year of a course is interpreted as 2 terms (2 semesters or 2 quarters). Students on the quarter system are encouraged to complete 3 quarters of a sequence if their program offers it (e.g. Real Analysis a/b/c).
Beyond this, we look holistically for a variety of advanced coursework to demonstrate mastery of foundational material.
Are GRE scores required to apply?
No. We do not require GRE scores. If you choose to include the GRE mathematics subject test in your application, we will factor your score into our review. However we do not consider the GRE general test or other subject tests as part of our application review.
However, students coming from lesser known schools or with non-traditional paths are encouraged to include a GRE mathematics subject test score in their applications.
Who should write my letters of recommendation?
Letters should come from mathematics faculty who have taught you for at least 1 semester in the past 3 years.
Ideally, all three letters should come from faculty in Mathematics departments at institutions of higher learning who have known the applicant for at least one full semester. Letters from graduate student TAs, high school teachers, coaches, spiritual leaders, or co-workers are not appropriate.
At least one letter should come from a faculty member under whom you have conducted research in mathematics.
We understand that some applicants come to us from non-traditional paths which make it impossible to meet these guidelines. If that is the case, then please do your best to meet the spirit of these guidelines, and also please consider submitting a GRE Mathematics Subject Test score.
What is the most critical/important part of the application?
Reviewers evaluate applications holistically, meaning every part is important and given due consideration. Different applicants have different strengths that distinguish them as excellent fits for our program. We look forward to reading about all of your achievements.
Can you tell me if my application will be competitive before I apply?
Unfortunately, no. The review committee cannot pre-screen applicants.
Our program is highly selective, but we do consider applicants holistically. If you exceed our minimum requirements for GPA and coursework, and you have a strong passion for mathematics, then we encourage you to apply.
What is the acceptance rate for PhD programs?
We are a small department and hence have small incoming classes. Unfortunately, this means we often turn down exceptional students whom we would otherwise love to admit.
Our combined PhD program aims for an incoming class of 12-15 students each Fall, giving a total PhD student population of about 70 students.
My interests intersect both Pure mathematics and Applied Mathematics. Should I apply for both programs?
The difference between the Mathematics and the Applied Mathematics program is whether or not students have a background in Algebra and plan to take the Algebra course (required by the Pure Mathematics program). There is no advantage to applying to both programs. Applicants will not be reviewed twice, even if applying to both programs. We do not have quotas for admissions ratios between the two programs, just an overall limit on our number of combined admissions. Please choose the program based on your experience and your interests.
